description: core §7.5, a heartbeat's time under a deployment epoch (core §7.6, §8.6), and the time freshness.v2 §2.4's and §2.10's owner writes. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked by a second, never blessed. Every case is layouts.json's `bare.v1`, a revision with no collection, so a body is its time alone: 32 bits of seconds from the deployment epoch, 10 of milliseconds, then 6 of pad (`bodies.json`). `epoch` is the deployment epoch in seconds, the catalog's the owner is given; where none is given, E = 0, as an owner with no catalog counts from the Unix epoch. `at` is an instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, `utc` the same instant in RFC 3339, or `null` for an owner whose clock reads no instant. `guard` is `true` while the owner's clock guard holds (core §4.3), and absent otherwise. `writes`: an epoch, an instant and the guard → the time as `bodies.json` spells it (`{"s", "ms"}`, `null` for the unknown time, all 42 bits set, or `"ahead"` for the ahead time, the seconds all ones and the millisecond code 1022), the body's `bits` before the pad, the `pad` and the `hex` bytes. While the guard holds the owner writes the ahead time, whatever its clock reads. Otherwise an instant before the epoch, or 2^32 seconds or more after it, has no code, and the owner writes the unknown time. `reads`: an epoch and a body's bytes → the instant, `at` and `utc`; `{"at": null}` for the unknown time; `{"ahead": true}` for the ahead time, which carries no instant; or `{"refused": "code"}` for an unused millisecond code: 1000 to 1021 under any seconds, and 1022 or 1023 under seconds that are not all ones (`bodies.json` holds the other refusals). Seconds all ones with a millisecond code up to 999 are a known time. Every write whose time is known reads back to its `at`. `earlier`, where a case states it, is what a reader built before the ahead time answers for the same bytes. It is no expectation of this text: it shows that such a reader refuses the body, so the heartbeat confirms nothing to it.
